newsitem.title: INDIA: India coalition names nominee for vice-president.
newsitem.headline: India coalition names nominee for vice-president.

text.p: India's ruling United Front coalition and its main ally the Congress party on Saturday named Krishan Kant, governor of the southern state of Andhra Pradesh, as its candidate for the post of the country's vice-president.
"We are happy that a consensus has been reached on the name of Krishan Kant from the United Front and also from the Congress side," the United Front's Chandrababu Naidu told a news conference.

Prime Minister Inder Kumar Gujral told the same news conference he hoped opposition parties would also support the candidature of Krishan Kant, a constitutional expert who took part in India's campaign for freedom from British rule.
Former vice-president K.R. Narayanan, who was supported by all the country's major political parties, took office as the country's 10th president on Friday.
The vice-president wields no real powers but steps into the president's shoes in his absence. He also chairs Parliament's upper house, the Rajya Sabha.
